title: Brass personnel changes and Moore as lead trombone
summary: Welburn asks about the changing brass section on the 1946 recordings; Moore says he led the trombone section.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I see. Okay. Let's see you made some recordings later in the year with the Louie Armstrong orchestra and noting from the discography there was a change in personnel, especially in the trumpet section and in the trombone section. There's always changes in personnel but it seems that the trumpet and trombone people this time were the ones that were replaced or left the orchestra for one reason or another, while the reed section stayed intact. Joe Garland was in that. Don Hill, John Sparrow and Amos Gordon Ernest Thompson, they all stayed together but much of the brass section changed. You were the one remaining member, as a matter of fact from that first recording session, brass section. What happened there?

Well, at different times when a man would come in from a tour back in New York, invariably some of the brass men, I don't know how it turned out that way -- would leave. Maybe they couldn't stand the road or anything like that. I always played the first trombone with Louie and I would take charge of the trombone section and different guys would come in andout, I guess they were tired of the road --

So you were the lead trombonist and you had to coordinate a lot of the activities of the trombone section as far as their work is concerned?
Of course up until the time I was with Louie with the big band, many trombonists would come and go, our section along with the brass, always had nice trumpet players.

Well, the band sounds good on those two tracks that you were involved in, "Endie" and "The Blues are Brewing." Your lead trombone is very much there, very much your full part of the ensemble was leading the trombone section, fills out the sound very well. You had that projection there. Have you been satisfied with those recordings and your contribution to them over the years?
Yes, yes, I didn't mention it, but Billy Holiday was in the picutre and she same "Andy" in that picture.
Remember that? She sang it beautifully.
Did you get a chance to play any solos on those particular selections when you would

Well, at one time we had a guy by the name of, small guy, tenor player, by the name of Bill Moore and Bill Moore used to do this specialty in front of the band, too, just Bill Moore and myself and sometimes when time warrants, like if there's time to -- there's certain amount of minutes in each show, stage show that if there's too many acts I wouldn't get a chance to do my solo. But most of the time I would do my solo, whatever I would do. I was a part of the Armstrong unit. I would either do the show or, you know, just lay out because there's enough acts to carry out the minutes of the show.
